newsitem.title: USA: BT to buy Raymond for $33/shr.
newsitem.headline: BT to buy Raymond for $33/shr.

text.p: BT Industries AB of Sweden said Monday it will buy Raymond Corp for $33 per share in cash.

Raymond's board of directors unanimously approved the agreement, which provides for a tender offer for all outstanding Raymond shares by Lift Acquisition Co., a wholly-owned subsidiary of BT, the companies said in a joint statement.
Raymond's shares closed at 35-1/8 on Friday, June 13, more than two points over BT's offer. They opened at 32-5/8, down 2-1/2, on Monday.

Ross Colquhoun, Raymond's chief executive, said in a statement the $33 per share deal represented "excellent value to our shareholders." He added BT's offer represented a 27 percent premium over Raymond's stock price on February 28, when the company said it intended to boost shareholder value.
Colquhoun or other Raymond officials were unavailable for comment.

The company, a supplier of transport and storage equipmen reported profits of $0.41 per share in the first quarter ended March 31, down from $0.45 a year earlier. Raymond had about $10.8 million common shares outstanding on March 31.
BT is a manufacturer of lift trucks and related equipment with 1996 revenues of about $600 million in revenues, the statement said.
Salomon Brothers acted as financial advisor to BT in the transaction, and Lehman Brothers Holdings Inc to Raymond, the statment said.
